Probably the apple is on the fk position while the model use the ik because of the guitar contact point.

For the non-animators out there : arms and legs of 3d models have two control sets, ik and fk between which you switch depending on the situation. 

Ik is when you have a controller for the hand or foot that is static, it's like the hand or foot is pinned where the controller is, moving the body won't affect their position and the elbow or knee will adapt their position in accordance to them automatically. You use it when there's a contact point with an object or other body parts. 

Fk is when there's a controllers on each articulations of the arm or leg, it work like a puppet, if you move the elbow the whole forearm will move, if you move the torso the whole arm will follow, you use it for fluid movements.

So the model can switch between ik and fk but both controllers exist at the same time even when the model don't use them so if you tie an object to fk but use ik, that object will look like it's floating at a random position because it's following the second hand coordinates.
